title: HiTF: A Hippocampal-Thalamic Function-Inspired Framework for Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Data

problem.claim: Multimodal sentiment analysis with random frame-level missingness is hindered by fragmented emotional cues and heterogeneous data quality.

gap.claim: Existing completion methods often neglect residual modality specificity and cross-modal reliability, leading to redundancy.

contributions.claim: HiTF is a brain-function-inspired framework for multimodal sentiment analysis with incomplete data.
The hippocampal-inspired intra-modal enhancement stream uses memory retrieval and sparse activation to mine modality-specific semantics and reconstruct missing information.
The thalamic-inspired inter-modal regulation stream evaluates modality reliability to adaptively integrate high-quality cross-modal information while suppressing redundant interference.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS report 1.5%–-2.5% average accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art methods across all missing rates.
Under a 90% missing condition on MOSI, the framework reports substantial F1-score improvements over strong baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis is challenged by random frame-level missingness, fragmented cues, and heterogeneous data quality.
Existing completion methods may overlook modality-specific information and cross-modal reliability.
Hippocampal pattern completion and thalamic reliability-based multisensory regulation motivate the framework.
HiTF combines intra-modal enhancement for reconstruction with inter-modal regulation for reliability-aware integration.
The authors report improvements across three datasets and under an extreme 90% missing condition on MOSI.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates modality-specific reconstruction from reliability-aware cross-modal integration.

interpretation.claim: Robust multimodal processing may benefit from treating within-modality recovery and cross-modality fusion as complementary responsibilities.

application.claim: For incomplete multimodal systems, consider dedicated mechanisms for recovering modality-specific semantics and filtering unreliable or redundant cross-modal signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation is necessary or effective outside the reported sentiment-analysis datasets and missingness settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baseline identities, evaluation protocols, or statistical significance of the reported improvements.
The abstract does not provide ablation results separating the two streams or their individual mechanisms.
The abstract does not provide implementation, computational-cost, or reproducibility details.
